references.text: Moses repeats the command regarding just weights and measures in his farewell message to Israel, emphasizing the importance of honesty in trade.
Proverbs confirms that a false weight is an abomination to the Lord, while accurate weights are pleasing to him.
Shows that correct weights and balances come from the Lord, and all the weights in the bag are his work.
Warns against using different weights and measures, as this is an abomination to the Lord.
Ezekiel prophesies about the restoration of just weights and measures in future Israel.
Amos condemns those who use false measures and weights to deceive the poor.
Micah condemns unjust measures and false weights as abominations.
God's self-presentation as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt, the same basis for obedience as in Leviticus.
Repeats the formula that the Lord is Israel's God who brought them out of Egypt.
